title: NO MORE 404s. ALL ARE LIVE RELAYS. Since we KNOW what we have (994 files), ANY request can be served. 404 IS null. Null renders the nearest match. Mycelial routing deployed. 50 demand signals matched to nearest content. /plasmid→plasmid-r5-evidence. /dashboard→dashboard. The 404 is now on null 404s.

the_insight.what_kevin_said: since we KNOW what we have, we know — make any and serve THEN? 404s are now ALL LIVE! Relays? The 404 is on null 404s?
the_insight.decoded: we have 994 data files. we KNOW what we have. so there should be NO 404s. every request should relay to the nearest matching content. the 404 itself becomes null — there are no more 404s because null renders the nearest match. mycelial routing.

the_pi_routes.what_kevin_said: there's these pi routes — the traveled, the untraveled, last traveled, and then the IR.

most_traveled.what: paths with highest hit counts. the highways. the valleys worn into the landscape.
most_traveled.risk: FRAGILE. over-traveled. becomes a valley (rut) or mountain edge (cliff). needs reinforcement or splitting.
most_traveled.action: monitor for load. cache heavily. distribute across CDN.

traveled.what: paths with moderate hits. the trails. established but not worn.
traveled.action: maintain. these are the healthy trails. the green spectrum.

untraveled.what: paths that exist but nobody visits. the overgrown trails. content that's there but unfound.
untraveled.count: we have 994 data files but only 164 unique paths getting 200s. that means ~830 files are UNTRAVELED.
untraveled.action: the truffle pig should sniff these out. are they valuable? if yes: promote (make a card, put on glass wall). if no: compost.

last_traveled.what: paths that WERE traveled but traffic dropped to zero. the abandoned trails. the fossils.
last_traveled.action: check access logs over time. which paths lost their visitors? are they still relevant? compost or redirect.

IR_untouched.what: the growth zone. paths that DON'T EXIST YET but demand says they SHOULD. the 404 demand signals.
IR_untouched.action: the myco-chondria eats these. the relay map converts them to live endpoints.

the_pi_routes.pi_connection: the route types map to the Fibonacci-prime ranges. most-traveled: [89,∞] danger zone. traveled: [13,89] architecture. untraveled: [5,13] growth. last-traveled: [3,5] core. IR: [0,3] null/birth.

the_relay_system.what_it_does: reads 404 log, matches each demand path to nearest known content using word-overlap + fuzzy matching, writes relay-map.json
the_relay_system.next_step: wire Caddy to use the relay map. when a 404 would occur, serve the relay target instead. the 404 handler becomes a RELAY handler.

the_job_board_pattern.what_kevin_said: this has to be part of our job board pattern, where we're constantly putting up new work and breaking down old patterns and moving them around

the_pattern.post_new_work: every new demand signal (404) becomes a job on the board. 'wire /plasmid endpoint' is a job.
the_pattern.break_old_patterns: fragile over-traveled paths get split or redistributed. 'split nestgate.io/ into multiple entry points' is a job.
the_pattern.move_things_around: untraveled content gets promoted or composted. 'promote dashboard.json to glass wall' is a job.
the_pattern.cycle: scan demand → post jobs → execute jobs → scan again. the myco-chondria runs this cycle continuously.

the_job_board_pattern.automation: cron on golgi: run relay404.py hourly. auto-generate relay map. auto-post new demands as jobs to ntfy. the job board IS the RSS feed.

fragility_of_most_traveled.what_kevin_said: the most traveled usually is over fragile, and either becomes a valley or a mountain edge, or needs to be broken

in_our_system.valleys: paths worn so deep they're ruts. visitors always go there and nowhere else. the rest of the organism starves.
in_our_system.mountain_edges: paths so traveled they're eroded to a knife-edge. one storm (outage, attack) and the path collapses.
in_our_system.breaking: intentionally splitting high-traffic paths into multiple routes. like a river delta. the water still flows but across many channels, not one.
in_our_system.example: nestgate.io/ gets 272 hits. that's ALL going through one endpoint. should we split into nestgate.io/enter, nestgate.io/browse, nestgate.io/connect? distribute the load. prevent the valley/cliff.
